dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Adds concrete, up‑to‑date 2026 pricing numbers, break‑even I/O formula (storage_GB × 0.4 M I/O), ACU cost ($0.12/h), and detailed decision matrices that a generic model would not know off‑hand. However, much of the content restates well‑known Aurora cost concepts, so it does not reach the absolute maximum.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Provides an AWS‑specific, ordered workflow (data gate → Cost Explorer reconciliation → right‑sizing → I/O tier → RI → etc.) and concrete CLI commands. A few steps (e.g., generic "Validate input") are not uniquely AWS‑specific, preventing a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Contains a thorough NEVER list with explicit rationales (e.g., never switch I/O tier without break‑even calc, never drop Serverless min‑capacity below SLA). Missing a few niche pitfalls (e.g., subtle cost of cross‑region Global DB traffic) keeps it just shy of full marks.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Frontmatter is complete, description, keywords, activation triggers, invocation schema, and a minimal example are all present and well‑formed. An agent can reliably know when and how to invoke the skill.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: The document layers high‑level purpose, strict output contract, quick start, then deep step‑by‑step logic, which is good. However, the early sections (mindset, quick reference) are dense and contain many details that could overload the reader before they know the top‑level trigger.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Destructive actions are tightly constrained: mandatory CONFIRM, snapshot, one‑dimension‑per‑maintenance‑window, batch size limit of 3 clusters. Perfect calibration for fragility.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a recognizable CloudOps skill pattern (overview → contract → mindset → process steps → anti‑patterns → navigation). Minor ad‑hoc ordering of some sections prevents a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Model output shows several execution gaps: (1) mis‑calculated I/O‑Optimized savings ($20 vs expected $40), (2) missing required monthly savings lines (right‑sizing, storage, etc.) in some blocks, (3) inconsistent cost numbers across blocks, (4) occasional omission of confidence rationale details. These errors would cause an agent to produce incorrect or incomplete optimisation reports.
